import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Stochastic_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 5  # sources
    J = 10  # destinations
    S = 15  # scenarios
    alpha = 0.9  # confidence level
    max_violations = int(math.floor((1 - alpha) * S))

    supplies = [126, 128, 143, 102, 113]
    recourse_caps = [50, 51, 57, 40, 45]
    base_costs = [[8.32, 9.62, 21.77, 11.85, 23.07, 24.19, 13.06, 18.68, 10.55, 13.68], [21.74, 24.83, 7.38, 23.11, 15.79, 6.54, 14.84, 5.24, 22.44, 24.87], [13.83, 5.38, 20.91, 21.15, 20.92, 16.65, 18.3, 18.86, 5.4, 24.41], [9.73, 14.37, 24.57, 6.6, 8.74, 14.62, 18.43, 7.1, 14.19, 20.41], [16.83, 11.18, 16.6, 7.9, 6.98, 19.9, 19.72, 16.45, 13.86, 13.15]]
    recourse_costs = [[16.64, 19.24, 43.54, 23.7, 46.14, 48.38, 26.12, 37.36, 21.1, 27.36], [43.48, 49.66, 14.76, 46.22, 31.58, 13.08, 29.68, 10.48, 44.88, 49.74], [27.66, 10.76, 41.82, 42.3, 41.84, 33.3, 36.6, 37.72, 10.8, 48.82], [19.46, 28.74, 49.14, 13.2, 17.48, 29.24, 36.86, 14.2, 28.38, 40.82], [33.66, 22.36, 33.2, 15.8, 13.96, 39.8, 39.44, 32.9, 27.72, 26.3]]
    demand_scenarios = [[12, 32, 14, 38, 11, 28, 47, 53, 17, 42], [12, 52, 23, 49, 19, 26, 36, 46, 23, 43], [11, 47, 20, 39, 19, 35, 50, 56, 25, 32], [11, 48, 19, 53, 11, 28, 53, 47, 28, 38], [11, 33, 23, 43, 18, 38, 56, 33, 26, 31], [9, 52, 17, 56, 17, 36, 43, 49, 25, 38], [13, 43, 18, 45, 13, 34, 38, 42, 16, 47], [10, 31, 21, 48, 17, 35, 31, 34, 27, 42], [10, 38, 18, 58, 14, 44, 52, 50, 20, 31], [15, 31, 15, 37, 19, 39, 55, 44, 28, 28], [13, 34, 18, 61, 11, 37, 51, 56, 20, 43], [11, 30, 18, 48, 17, 38, 34, 41, 17, 31], [11, 50, 16, 46, 19, 46, 36, 35, 20, 35], [10, 52, 13, 59, 16, 43, 51, 49, 21, 30], [14, 45, 17, 38, 12, 43, 46, 58, 28, 36]]

    # Big-M: largest demand * 2
    M = max(demand_scenarios[s][j] for s in range(S) for j in range(J)) * 2

    # --- Variables ---
    # Stage 1: base shipments
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Base_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Stage 2: recourse shipments per scenario
    y = {}
    for s in range(S):
        for i in range(I):
            for j in range(J):
                y[(i,j,s)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Recourse_S{i}_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # Violation indicators
    z = {}
    for j in range(J):
        for s in range(S):
            z[(j,s)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Violate_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # --- Objective: minimize base cost + expected recourse cost ---
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(base_costs[i][j] * x[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J))
        + (1.0 / S) * quicksum(recourse_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j,s)]
                               for s in range(S) for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply (base)
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"SupplyBase_S{i}")

    # C2: Supply (recourse per scenario)
    for i in range(I):
        for s in range(S):
            m.addConstr(
                quicksum(y[(i,j,s)] for j in range(J)) <= recourse_caps[i],
                name=f"SupplyRecourse_S{i}_Sc{s}")

    # C3: Demand chance constraint (SAA)
    for j in range(J):
        for s in range(S):
            m.addConstr(
                quicksum(x[(i,j)] + y[(i,j,s)] for i in range(I))
                + M * z[(j,s)] >= demand_scenarios[s][j],
                name=f"DemandChance_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # C4: Violation budget per destination
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(z[(j,s)] for s in range(S)) <= max_violations,
            name=f"ViolationBudget_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Leadership Team
From: Supply Chain Director
Date: [Insert date]
Subject: Phased shipping plan to manage demand uncertainty and protect service levels

Challenge
Our warehouse-to-store network faces variable customer demand from period to period. If we ship too little in advance, we risk stockouts, lost sales, and rushed replenishments at premium rates. If we ship too much, we overcommit inventory and freight capacity where it may not be needed. We must set a reliable plan before demand is known, and then respond quickly once actuals are revealed.

Phased approach
We will use a phased strategy that separates proactive positioning from reactive adjustments:
- Base plan: Pre-position inventory from warehouses to stores ahead of the demand period. This plan is locked in before demand is known and respects available inventory and regular transportation capacity. It should cover the bulk of expected needs across the forecast scenarios.
- Emergency adjustments: After demand is observed, deploy urgent shipments to stores with shortfalls. These shipments carry higher unit costs and must respect separate surge capacity limits. Emergency moves are targeted and used only where gaps appear.

Reliability target
We will fully satisfy each store’s demand in at least the agreed service-level share of forecast scenarios across the planning horizon. Shortfalls are acceptable in the small residual tail of scenarios, with a clear mitigation playbook for those cases. This balances service commitments with prudent use of higher-cost emergency transport.

Cost objective
Our goal is to keep the expected total cost as low as possible while sustaining the service-level commitment. Total cost combines:
- The committed spend from the base shipping plan, and
- The average emergency shipping spend across the forecast scenarios.
We will assess the trade-off between a leaner base plan that may require more emergency shipments and a more generous base plan that reduces emergency exposure but ties up capacity.

Operational guardrails
- Base shipments will not exceed on-hand or pre-allocated inventory at each warehouse.
- Emergency shipments will observe separate surge capacity limits and carrier availability.
- Store-level service will be measured across the full set of demand scenarios at the agreed confidence level.
- For scenarios where shortfalls are permitted, we will define clear actions (e.g., prioritized SKU substitutions, customer communication, and expedited replenishment windows).

Next steps
- Confirm the service-level policy by store.
- Validate and finalize the set of forecast demand scenarios and stress cases.
- Confirm base and emergency cost structures and available capacities.
- Draft an initial base shipping plan and test it across all scenarios to measure service reliability and expected cost.
- Iterate on allocations and emergency triggers until we reach the best-performing plan under the defined guardrails.
- Establish monitoring and decision checkpoints to execute the base plan and activate emergency shipments when needed.
